scope: Hatoyama Hall in Otowa, Tokyo, in 2006. The house includes the west stone porte-cochère and arched entry, the projecting south garden rooms and the roof of the reinforced-concrete mansion.

primaryWrittenSources.facts: The museum identifies Okada Shinichirō’s 1924 reinforced-concrete mansion and its English-inspired exterior facing a rose garden.
The museum identifies the west carriage porch and stair hall, south sunroom and upper balcony.
The architectural account describes two main floors over a basement, masonry-look walls, and white frames and ornament.
The architectural account specifies arched lower openings and four-leaf sliders with Western railings on the upper south sunroom.
